reasons: The lake identity record is Oliver v. United States, decided by the U.S. Supreme Court on 1984-04-17.
The official citation in the lake record is 466 U.S. 170, matching the content page citation and the asserted display citation.

defect.evidence_quote: It is not generally true that fences or “No Trespassing” signs effectively bar the public from viewing open fields in rural areas.
defect.locator_note: pin-179b; opinion text at page marker *179.
defect.problem: The quote truncates the opinion sentence and changes it into a complete sentence without ellipsis; the opinion says the public is not effectively barred from viewing open fields "in rural areas."
defect.proposed_fix: Use the full sentence: "It is not generally true that fences or “No Trespassing” signs effectively bar the public from viewing open fields in rural areas."

reasons: The lake pinpoint itself marks quote_fidelity as mismatch.
The disclosed opinion text contains the sentence with the additional words "in rural areas" and curly quotation marks around “No Trespassing”.
residual_risks: The substantive proposition is supported, but the verbatim quotation is not character-faithful.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Quote the full sentence exactly or mark the omission with an ellipsis.

defect.evidence_quote: In contrast, open fields do not provide the setting for those intimate activities that the Amendment is intended to shelter from government interference or surveillance.
defect.locator_note: pin-179; content line 55; opinion text at page marker *179.
defect.problem: The asserted quote is not opinion text; it appears to be a malformed harvest from the page text around the Issue/Rule headings.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace the stored pin quote with the actual page-179 opinion passage supporting the rule.

reasons: The asserted quote is "signs, and secluded. ## Rule Yes.", which does not appear as a holding passage in the disclosed opinion text.
The lake pinpoint marks quote_fidelity as mismatch.
residual_risks: The content page's displayed rule quote is substantively located at page 179, but the lake pinpoint quote is unusable as verbatim evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Store the exact opinion sentence, or if using the page's partial quote, ensure the alteration and omission are explicit and tied to the page-179 text.

defect.evidence_quote: the common law distinguished “open fields” from the “curti-lage,” the land immediately surrounding and associated with the home.
defect.locator_note: pin-180; opinion text at page marker *180.
defect.problem: The quote is not character-faithful: the disclosed text uses curly double quotation marks, OCR hyphenates “curti-lage,” and ends the clause with a period after "home" rather than a comma.
defect.proposed_fix: Use the exact disclosed text or normalize only outside quotation marks; do not present a modified passage as verbatim.

reasons: The lake pinpoint marks quote_fidelity as mismatch.
The asserted quote changes quotation marks, dehyphenates the disclosed text, and changes the terminal punctuation from period to comma.
residual_risks: The substantive curtilage distinction is supported, but this exact quotation is not faithful to the disclosed text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If dehyphenating the OCR text to "curtilage," avoid treating the passage as character-exact, or cite a verified reporter source that supports the normalized wording.

reasons: Treatment/currency is outside lens A's attack charter.

The asserted treatment fields match the disclosed lake treatment fields: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 1984-04-17, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, varies_by_point false, and the same scope note.
residual_risks: No independent treatment audit performed under lens A.
